ghi_chu: Video dài Chu Du có thật sự bị Gia Cát Lượng chọc tức đến chết

nhan_vat.zy: Zhou Yu at about thirty-three, a handsome slim man with fine features, a thin moustache and a short neat beard, black hair in a topknot under a plain black cap, a plain solid dark teal long robe, a simple leather chest guard, a plain dark sash, empty hands
nhan_vat.zyy: young Zhou Yu at about twenty-four, handsome and clean-shaven, black topknot, a plain solid dark teal robe with a plain sash, empty hands
nhan_vat.sc: Sun Ce at about twenty-four, a stocky energetic young man with a short stubble beard and a broad grin, a plain solid dark maroon robe with a plain dark sash, empty hands
nhan_vat.sq: Sun Quan at about twenty-six, a young ruler with a square face and a short beard, a purple silk robe with embroidered gold dragon-pattern borders and a jade belt, a tall black ceremonial cap, empty hands
nhan_vat.cc: Cao Cao at about fifty-three, a short wiry man with sharp clever eyes, a thin moustache and a small beard with a few grey hairs, a plain solid dark-grey robe with a plain sash, a tall black cap, empty hands, no weapon
nhan_vat.hg: Huang Gai, a tough old general of about sixty with a grey beard and weathered face, a plain solid dark brown robe under simple leather armour, empty hands
nhan_vat.ls: Lu Su, a stout calm man of about thirty-seven with a round kind face and a plain moustache, a plain solid dark olive-green robe, empty hands
nhan_vat.zgl: Zhuge Liang at about twenty-seven, a tall slim man with a calm intelligent smile and a thin moustache, a plain solid off-white undyed hemp robe with a plain dark-blue sash, a cloth scarf cap, empty hands
nhan_vat.cr: Cao Ren, a stern general of about fifty with a square jaw and a short black beard, a plain solid dark red-brown robe with a simple leather chest guard
nhan_vat.cp: Cheng Pu, an old rugged officer with a grey beard and a scarred cheek, a plain solid dark umber-brown robe with a simple leather chest guard
nhan_vat.lb: Liu Bei at about forty-eight, a mild man with long earlobes and a faint moustache, a plain solid dark green robe, empty hands
nhan_vat.gy: Guan Yu, a tall man with a very long black beard and a red face, a plain solid dark green robe, empty hands
nhan_vat.zf: Zhang Fei, a burly broad-faced man with a short bristling black beard and wide eyes, a plain solid dark indigo-blue robe, empty hands
nhan_vat.ps: Pei Songzhi, an elderly annotator of about sixty with a thin grey beard, a plain solid dark slate-grey robe with a black cap, gentle focused face
nhan_vat.cs: Chen Shou, a calm scholar-historian of about fifty in a plain solid dark indigo robe and black cap, thoughtful face
nhan_vat.kc: a Han street storyteller of about fifty, thin face, short grey beard, a plain brown long robe, a cloth headband tied over a topknot, a small hand drum tucked under one arm, expressive open hands
nhan_vat.dan: townspeople of different ages and faces in plain solid-colour tunics in dark indigo, dark brown, dark olive, maroon and charcoal, each face different
nhan_vat.sb: a Han soldier in a plain solid dark grey or dark olive tunic with a simple leather chest guard, simple face

canh.mo_ta: a brilliant victory at sunrise on a broad river: sailors on the deck of a boxy Han flagship cheering with raised arms, the burnt wreck of an enemy fleet drifting behind, and at the centre a general in dark teal standing proudly among his men, golden light on the water

a Han market square where a crowd of townspeople gathers around a laughing storyteller who stands behind a low wooden platform with a hand drum, on the platform in front of him two stiff carved wooden puppets, each as tall as a forearm, with a painted adult face, straight jointed wooden limbs and a tiny cap: a puppet in a dark teal robe lying on its back and a taller puppet in a white robe with a blue border standing over it, the townspeople gasping and pointing

in the foreground Zhou Yu seated on a mat at a low table with a tight jaw and narrowed jealous eyes, and behind him through the open tent flap Zhuge Liang in white calmly speaking to a group of listening officers who nod with respect

two men sit across a low table in a tent playing a board game with flat black and white stones: on the left Zhuge Liang, tall and lean with a thin moustache, in a plain off-white hemp robe and a cloth scarf cap, calmly placing a stone; on the right Zhou Yu, older and broader with a short dark beard, in a dark teal robe and a black cap, frowning with a stone in his fingers

Zhou Yu staggering backward clutching his chest with a pained face while exactly two officers rush in, one officer holding him under his left arm and the other under his right arm, a calm riverside camp at dusk behind them

a Han storyteller, a thin grey-bearded man in a brown robe, stands behind a low wooden table in a market square; on the table stand four tiny carved wooden chess-piece-like figures in a row, each only as tall as his hand, simple blank-faced wooden figurines in off-white, olive-green, dark teal and maroon painted cloth, all standing upright; a few townspeople of different ages watch

a thoughtful townsman with one hand on his chin and a doubtful raised eyebrow, a large glowing golden question-mark floating in the air above his head, a curious child beside him tugging his sleeve and looking up at the question-mark, a quiet Han street behind them in soft daylight

a three-storey Han tower seen from outside in bright daylight: the ground floor is a sturdy stone archive with a keeper standing beside neatly tied bundles, the middle floor is an open wooden hall where three scholars crowd over a table adding small bundles to larger ones, the top floor is an open painted stage with colourful cloth streamers where a storyteller spreads his arms before a cheering crowd

a mother holding a swaddled baby at the doorway of a well-off Han country house in Lujiang, her husband standing beside her with a proud smile, rice fields and green hills behind, two clearly different faces
two young men of the same age side by side under a tree, arms on each other's shoulders, laughing, Zhou Yu slim in a dark teal robe and Sun Ce stocky in a red-brown robe, clearly different faces

Zhou Yu opening the gate of a big courtyard mansion and sweeping his sleeve to invite Sun Ce in, Sun Ce bowing in thanks, a big house with tiled roofs on the south side of a country road, two different faces

young Zhou Yu walking out of the big mansion gate carrying a small cloth bundle with a light easy smile, while behind him in the courtyard Sun Ce stands cheerfully with a rolled sleeping mat under his arm, two different faces and robes

a banquet hall with musicians: Zhou Yu holding a two-eared bronze wine cup turning his head sharply to look over his shoulder at a zither player who has played a wrong note and looks guilty, other guests unaware, three different faces

a long low zither lying on a table beside a sand-table of a river valley: wavy golden ribbons of sound rise from the zither strings and flow across the table turning into tiny flags and little clay soldiers arranged in a battle formation, Zhou Yu in dark teal leaning over the table with a keen listening look and two officers watching
winter on the north bank of a wide river, a vast column of Cao army soldiers with plain blank banners marching down toward the water through light snow, tiny figures, wide view, grey sky

Cao Cao standing on a tall earthen platform with one arm raised proclaiming to an enormous army of grown men in dense disciplined ranks spread across the riverbank to the horizon, spearmen and archers, plain blank banners, wind in his sleeves

Zhou Yu and two officers around a sand-table of a river valley counting with small clay markers: a small group of tired grey markers on the north bank and a larger group of green markers apart on the east side, the three men leaning over the table with focused faces

a rank of southern surrendered soldiers standing apart from the others, glancing at each other and whispering uncertainly toward a distant flag made of one single flat red cloth, wary faces, each face different, soft light
Zhou Yu bowing with hands joined before Sun Quan who sits on a low mat in a hall and nods, Zhou Yu in a dark teal robe and Sun Quan in dark purple, clearly different faces, two attendants far behind
Zhou Yu on a horse leading a long column of thirty thousand soldiers along a riverside road toward a distant river town, plain blank banners, dust, wide view, soldiers small

a broad river seen from a high bank: on the right a vast crowded enemy fleet of boxy Han war-barges covering the whole water to the horizon, on the left a small compact fleet of only a few similar warships with tiny sailors on the decks, a calm general in dark teal on the nearest deck

on the deck of a boxy Han warship at dusk the old general Huang Gai points across the water to the enemy fleet whose ships lie tied close together in long rows, and Zhou Yu in dark teal beside him listens with a thoughtful nod
a row of small fast boats tied at a quay at dusk, sailors piling dry brushwood and straw onto them and pouring oil from clay jars, calm blue dusk sky, the boats unlit and the quay quiet
a line of small boats rushing across the middle of the river with sails swollen by a strong south-east wind, the lead boat's bow just catching flame, flags streaming, spray, dusk

the whole enemy fleet of boxy Han warships burning on a calm river at night, towering flames and black smoke filling the sky, the water mirroring the orange fire, the river empty apart from the burning boats, two officers stand on the dry bank at the far left watching
defeated soldiers trudging along a muddy road through reeds at night toward a distant walled city, plain lowered banners, small tired figures, smoke far behind, wide view
Zhou Yu on a wooden command tower dispatching orders with a firm outstretched arm while three officers kneel below to receive them, Zhou Yu in dark teal, officers clearly different faces

a Han street storyteller's low table: on it two small carved wooden puppets of grown men with stiff straight limbs, a small puppet in a dark teal robe and a taller puppet in an off-white robe; the storyteller, a thin grey-bearded man in a brown robe, lifts a small golden hat from the teal puppet and sets it on the white one; townspeople of different ages watch from behind

Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu standing side by side on a riverside mound looking across a wide river, Zhou Yu young and slim, Cheng Pu old with a grey beard, on the far bank the small camp of Cao Ren, clearly different faces

on a riverside mound Zhou Yu clutching his right side with a pained face, a single arrow lying on the ground at his feet, two officers hurrying to him from both sides to hold his arms, the wide river behind

Cao Ren on a horse before a line of assembled cavalry on a riverbank, pointing across the wide river at the far bank where a few enemy tents stand quietly in the morning light, the riders with different faces and plain blank banners

in a tent Zhou Yu pushing himself up from a low plank bed with one hand pressed to his side, an officer and a physician in plain robes supporting him on both sides, morning light through the open tent flap showing soldiers waiting outside

exactly ONE general on a horse: Cao Ren on the far river bank turning his horse away and raising one open hand, a plain blank cloth banner hanging from a tall pole planted firmly in the ground beside him, a few soldiers marching away behind, no second figure in front
evening torch light: Zhou Yu walking slowly through the camp past rows of soldiers who bow their heads to him, his hand pressed lightly to his side, determined face, soldiers with different faces

Zhou Yu and Liu Bei seated opposite each other at a low rectangular table on a riverside terrace at sunset, each holding a bronze wine cup, Guan Yu with his long black beard standing one step behind Liu Bei and an officer in dark teal one step behind Zhou Yu

Liu Bei seated uneasily on a mat in a grand palace hall, two court dancers in long sleeves dancing before him, and open wooden chests of jade and gold beside him, he looks uncomfortable; a plain flat red cloth screen hangs behind

Guan Yu and Zhang Fei standing outside a tall closed heavy wooden double gate looking anxiously toward it, while through a gap in the gate in the courtyard Liu Bei sits alone among silk bolts, three clearly different faces
Sun Quan seated on a mat shaking his head and waving a sleeve to refuse, Zhou Yu bowing before him with a disappointed face, two clearly different faces and robe colours

Zhou Yu and Lu Su bending over a sand-table model of a river city, on the model three small clay figures stand close together in a cluster and Zhou Yu's finger rests on the space between them and the city, thoughtful faces
Zhuge Liang speaking earnestly before Sun Quan seated on a mat in a hall, Zhou Yu standing aside with arms folded in his sleeves watching, three clearly different faces and robe colours

an old historian holding up a large blank unrolled strip of pale silk in a bright courtyard while three townsmen lean in and look for a story that is not there, one of them scratching his head and another raising an open palm in puzzlement
Zhou Yu pointing at a sand-table model of western mountains and rivers in a hall, Sun Quan listening with interest, two clearly different faces

an army column marching west through a high mountain pass, two leaders on horses at the front looking ahead: a bearded commander in dark teal on a brown horse, and a younger clean-shaven officer in dark blue-grey armour on a black horse, plain blank banners, steep cliffs, wide view, soldiers small
Zhou Yu and a younger officer on horseback on a ridge at sunrise looking west toward a far line of high mountains, a long army column resting on the slope below them, golden light
Zhou Yu in dark teal at the gate of Jiangling city giving orders while grown-man officers load wagons and soldiers line up, morning light, officers with different faces
a covered river boat with its curtains drawn gliding on a misty river at dusk, an officer standing at the stern with bowed head, soldiers marching along the bank, quiet sad mood

Zhou Yu lying pale on a low plank platform covered with a plain woven mat in a simple room, an old physician with a grey beard kneeling beside him and gently shaking his head, a steaming herbal bowl on a low plain table

an elderly annotator and two assistants at a wide low table comparing two pale silk cloths painted with a few brush-ink lines for rivers and small ink dots for towns, the old man pointing at one dot on the first silk while an assistant holds up the second silk, bright window light
exactly ONE man: Zhou Yu propped up in bed by a pillow roll, pale but resolute, writing carefully with a brush by the light of a Han bronze oil dish, no second figure
Zhou Yu seated on a low mat in a dim room handing a rolled bamboo-slip bundle tied with cord to a kneeling young messenger, pale face but firm eyes, two clearly different faces
Sun Quan in white mourning robes kneeling before a funeral hall hung with white cloth, tears on his face, two officers behind him moved and lowering their heads, three different faces

Sun Quan in white mourning robes standing beside a plain wooden coffin draped in white cloth with his hand resting on it and tears on his face, a row of officers in white bowing behind him in a bright hall
Sun Quan seated on a high dais speaking gravely, two rows of officers kneeling in the hall below, solemn and respectful mood, clearly different faces
Chen Shou the historian kneeling at a low table writing with a brush while two assistants kneel at his sides holding tied bamboo-slip bundles, a soft window light

a wall painter on a low wooden scaffold finishing a large painted mural of a standing man in a dark teal robe with a black cap and a dark leather chest guard, the painted standing man fills the middle of the plaster wall in bright colours, the painter beside the mural looking back thoughtfully, warm bright light, onlookers watching from below

a Han storyteller on a low plain wooden platform in a Han market square acting out a man clutching his chest and falling backward, a crowd of townspeople gasping and covering their mouths, a large glowing golden question-mark floating above the crowd
Zhuge Liang standing on a high rock in bright sunlight with a warm halo behind him, officers below looking up at him in awe, plain green blank banners, clear sky
Zhou Yu on a warship deck acclaimed by cheering soldiers raising their arms after a victory, the smoking wreck of an enemy fleet far behind, bright morning light, soldiers with different faces

a showman in a Han market square lifting a large golden jade ornament off the belt of a dark teal-robed figure and hanging it round the neck of a white-robed figure beside him, townspeople watching with interest, the dark teal figure looking down with a small dark cloud over his head

a Han street storyteller in a brown robe standing on a low wooden platform, raising one small off-white carved wooden puppet in his right hand to chest height and holding a small hand drum in his left, a small dark teal puppet lying on the platform before him, townspeople seen from behind watching

Zhou Yu standing in a street with a tight embarrassed face while exactly five townsfolk stand in a loose arc behind him, three whispering behind raised long sleeves and two shaking their heads, every townsperson with a different face and clothes

an open-air Han market square with a low wooden platform: a performer in a dark teal robe collapsing dramatically to the platform floor while a performer in a white-and-blue robe stands calmly with arms hidden in sleeves, an audience seen from behind

a Han market stage with three large bronze bells hanging in a row on a wooden frame, the storyteller striking the third bell with a wooden mallet while children in the front row clap in rhythm and hold up three fingers

an empty quiet riverbank at dusk shown as four things in a row from left to right: a single plain arrow with a bare wooden shaft standing upright in the earth, a small clay bowl of steaming herbal medicine on a low plain wooden stool, a wide river, and far away on the river a burning fleet of boxy Han warships glowing orange, one continuous picture of an uninhabited landscape

a three-storey Han tower under construction in bright daylight: workers and an old scholar pressing heavy square stone blocks into place to form the solid stone foundation and first floor, the upper floors still bare wooden frames, ropes and a wooden crane

at the stern of a warship at dusk Zhou Yu stands with one hand pressed lightly to his right side while soldiers around him look at him with respect, the burning remains of an enemy fleet glowing far behind on the water
Lu Su bowing before Sun Quan who wipes a tear with his sleeve, Lu Su stout in grey-green and Sun Quan in dark purple, a solemn hall, two clearly different faces

an old annotator with a thin grey beard kneeling at a low table, pointing at a plain brown cloth map drawn with only a few brush-drawn river lines, an assistant beside him holding a tied bundle of bamboo slips, a plain cloth windsock on a pole in the courtyard blowing from the east
Zhou Yu in the large foreground, red-faced with clenched fists and a furious expression, while far behind him Zhuge Liang stands small and calm with a gentle smile, sleeves hiding his hands

exactly ONE scholar sitting at a low table with two opened lacquered boxes beside him and a third box still closed and tied with cord in front of him, looking at the closed box thoughtfully, no second figure

a quiet room seen from the foot of a low plank bed: Zhou Yu lies on his back with his head on a single pillow and a blanket to his chest, eyes closed, a physician in a plain robe sitting beside the bed holding his wrist and an attendant standing at the door

a simple Han balance scale on a plain table, a plain wooden beam hung from a cord with a rope-hung bronze pan at each end: the left pan sagging low under several tied bundles of bamboo slips, the right pan high holding only a small wooden storyteller's block, soft window light, completely empty, absolutely no people

Zhou Yu standing calmly at the centre in dark teal, around him four glowing round medallion paintings floating in the air: a big courtyard house, a burning enemy fleet on a river, a wounded man standing up among watching soldiers, a man writing in a sickbed
a riderless horse with an empty saddle standing at the edge of a misty river at dawn facing distant western mountains, a few tiny officers far behind with bowed heads, quiet sad mood, wide view

seen from behind, exactly ONE townsman stands in the foreground of a dirt road that forks ahead into a wide Y, with one hand on his chin; the left fork runs down to a river where a few one-masted Han river boats burn with orange flames, the right fork runs to a small open wooden stage with a softly lit plain screen; one continuous landscape at dusk, no second figure

a street wall hung with three large painted cloth portraits of three clearly different men in Han robes: a young clean-shaven man, a middle-aged man with a beard and a white-haired old man with a long white beard; a woman and a boy stand before them looking up thoughtfully, bright afternoon light

a single shallow bronze oil dish on a low plain wooden table at dusk, its tiny flame bending low and small, through a plain square window opening in a thick mud-brick wall with fixed wooden bars in a grid, beyond it the glow of a burning fleet on the river fading to dark, completely empty, absolutely no people

a wide view from a hill over a vast riverside camp: countless small tents in endless rows and a packed crowd of small boats along the bank reaching the horizon, plain blank banners, tiny soldiers, cold winter light

a sand-table model of a river on a plain wooden table seen from above: on the right a huge field of tiny red clay markers, on the left a small group of tiny blue clay markers, a calm hand placing one blue marker, soft window light, only the hand visible

the first fire boats crashing into the enemy fleet of boxy Han warships at night, bright flames leaping from ship to ship, strong wind bending the flames, black smoke, small figures on the decks, wide view

in the foreground a plain empty reed mat with a neatly folded white scarf on it, behind it a bare wooden command tower made of plain timber posts with no signboard where Zhou Yu in dark teal gives orders and officers listen with different faces, bright daylight, the mat in the foreground is clearly empty

a plain wooden table with a sand-table model of western mountains and rivers: a pointer rests on a path that winds through a narrow gorge, one small clay city marker is left behind at the river and a second marker waits far to the west, bright warm light, completely empty, absolutely no people

two men standing side by side on a bright street: a tall man in a white robe with a blue border on a high wooden step beside a shorter dark teal-robed general on the lower level, townsmen with different faces look up at the white-robed man with admiration
a plain wooden table in bright light with three small wooden blocks standing in a row, the first two upright and the third knocked over on its side, completely empty, absolutely no people

a sand-table model of western mountains and rivers on a plain wooden table, a path marked with small flags only up to the middle and the remaining flags still lying in a wooden tray beside it, soft dawn light through a lattice window, completely empty, absolutely no people
